messages:
alex: quick idea — small SDK extension: introduce an opt-in `session-prefetch` mode for paged endpoints. goal: reduce tail latency for conversational pagination by speculatively fetching a short window of pages and gracefully degrading to single-page behavior on transport failures. sketch + tradeoffs below, seeking feedback.
Priya: high level user-visible semantics? failure & consistency model?
alex: user-visible: API surface stays `client.pages(req, ...)`. new opts: `prefetch_window` (int) and `session_budget_ms` (int). SDK will attempt to fetch up to `prefetch_window` pages ahead in the background and stash results. If prefetch fails (transport error, auth, route mismatch), SDK falls back to normal per-page fetching and emits telemetry + a flag on the session so apps can detect degraded experience.
Sam: duplication & idempotency concerns. If the SDK prefetches page N and later caller iterates to N, how do we avoid duplicate processing or double-charging?
alex: plan: local dedupe via a small in-memory page-anchor map keyed by a server-supplied stable page-id header when available. If server doesn't expose stable ids we use sequence numbers + best-effort dedupe and mark `prefetch_reliability: "best-effort"` in session metadata. We intentionally avoid changing server contracts. SDK will not reissue successful page requests if cached result exists.
michael: what about streaming transports vs unary RPCs? With streaming, ordering & head-of-line blocking make speculative reads thorny.
alex: implementation: prefer concurrent unary RPCs for prefetch (bounded worker pool). For streaming endpoints we open a short-lived auxiliary unary side-channel to request next pages; that side-channel must reuse the same routing/auth context. If side-channel unavailable, we simply disable prefetch for that session and log a warning.
Ira: metrics: `prefetch_hit_rate`, `prefetch_failure_rate`, `prefetch_degraded_sessions`, `prefetch_extra_token_cost`, and `session_id` for correlation. Also emit `prefetch_mode` in spans.
Priya: resource controls—browsers and mobile may not tolerate many concurrent prefetches. Defaults + caps?
alex: sensible defaults: `prefetch_window=1` (safe), `session_budget_ms=500`. Runtime caps: node=2, python=3, go=4 by default; configurable per-client. Also a hard global cap to avoid amplification during canaries.
Sam: retry policy: if prefetch retries aggressively we might spike backend load. How to be conservative?
alex: prefetch uses conservative backoff: at most one immediate retry with small jitter (e.g., 100ms) then stop. Consumer-facing per-page retries remain unchanged and authoritative. Prefetch is best-effort and low-cost.
michael: auth & routing: side-channel must reuse tokens and route metadata to preserve tenant affinity, else results may be invalid.
alex: agreed; SDK will attach identical routing metadata. If mismatch detected SDK cancels the prefetch and marks the session degraded.
ops-bot: rollout reminder: any change that introduces new default concurrency must have a perf bake, canary plan, and throttling switches. File a short rollout checklist.
Ira: propose an opt-in experiment flag `sdk.experimental.session_prefetch=true` for two weeks of telemetry before enabling by default. Also a kill-switch in client config and server-side feature gate to disable prefetch if needed.
Priya: can we see a minimal API example?
alex: example (py):
```
# existing
for page in client.pages(req):
    handle(page)

# with session-prefetch opts
for page in client.pages(req, prefetch_window=2, session_budget_ms=800):
    handle(page)
```

alex: followups: I'll draft a short RFC covering: API sketch, implementation plan per runtime (py/ts/go), telemetry + event shapes, perf goals (p99 latency reduction target and acceptable extra-token budget), and a canary/rollback checklist. If no objections, I'll ship the RFC tomorrow EOD. :thumbsup:
